name: Kiewit
summary: BOTTOM LINE UP FRONT: Kiewit is the power picks-and-shovels play on the AI buildout — a 142-year-old, employee-owned Omaha EPC giant now stacking a ~11 GW AI-driven gas-generation book: EPC on Homer City, PA (up to 4.5 GW, seven GE Vernova 7HA.02 turbines — the largest US gas plant under construction, powering a >3,200-acre AI campus), the NRG/GE Vernova venture (~5.4 GW of CCGTs for data-center demand in ERCOT/PJM), and Oglethorpe's 1,425 MW Georgia plant, plus lead-constructor on Oklo's first Aurora fast reactor at Idaho National Laboratory and completion of the 339-mile, 1,250 MW Champlain Hudson Power Express HVDC line. ENR ranks it #4 (2026) at $15.3B of ENR-counted revenue ($18.2B company-total with reported net income of $1,315M — a ~7.2% margin extraordinary for E&C), with the most diversified mix in the top 10 (38% power, 29% transportation). Its data-center practice sells the campus ecosystem — generation, transmission, water, modularization, >80% self-performed — not interior fit-out (only 4% telecom mix). Kiewit and Bechtel were both named delivery contractors under the $550B US-Japan AI infrastructure framework (October 2025). Watch items: Maryland dropped Kiewit from the ~$1.2B Key Bridge Phase 2 rebuild (April 2026, pricing 'far exceeding' state estimates), and the record fixed-price gas-EPC book concentrates execution risk against a constrained turbine supply chain. Collection gaps: no public backlog figure, no audited statements, no leadership page; the 2025 net-income figure is aggregator-sourced (medium confidence).
ecosystemRole: The electrons-and-infrastructure EPC of the AI era: while building GCs win the shells, Kiewit builds the gigawatt-class gas plants, HVDC lines, substations, water systems, and first SMRs that make AI campuses possible — self-performing more than 80% of the work with one of the industry's largest craft forces and equipment fleets.

productsAndServices.name: Power Generation EPC (the AI gas-power franchise)
productsAndServices.description: Kiewit Power Constructors and TIC (The Industrial Company, a wholly-owned subsidiary) deliver gas-fired generation at fleet scale: TIC cites >82,000 MW of gas-fired capacity delivered over the past decade including 35 combined-cycle projects. The AI cycle has stacked a ~11 GW book: Homer City (up to 4.5 GW), the NRG/GE Vernova venture (~5.4 GW), and Oglethorpe (1,425 MW).
highlights: Homer City Energy Campus, PA: EPC for up to 4.5 GW — 7x GE Vernova 7HA.02 hydrogen-enabled turbines on the former coal-plant site, powering a >3,200-acre AI/HPC campus; >$10B initial capex, power targeted 2027, >1,000 workers on site — the largest gas plant under construction in the US
NRG + GE Vernova + Kiewit (TIC) venture: ~5.4 GW of CCGTs for data-center demand in ERCOT and PJM — 1.2 GW by 2029, 1.2 GW by 2030, ~3 GW 2030-32, with reserved GEV turbine slots
Oglethorpe Power (GA): TIC selected as EPC for a 1,425 MW combined-cycle plant (GE Vernova 7HA.03; COD 2029; ~1,200 peak workers)
Reference CCGT fleet: TVA Cumberland 1,450 MW, Three Rivers 1,250 MW, Magnolia Unit 1 705 MW
productsAndServices.positioning: Reserved GE Vernova turbine slots plus proven 7HA-class EPC capability may be the tightest bottleneck asset in the AI-power complex — rivals can bid, but few can deliver gigawatt-class gas on 2027-29 schedules
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Fixed-price and progressive EPC contracts with developers, IPPs, utilities, and co-ops
productsAndServices.roadmap: Homer City first power 2027; NRG venture waves through 2032; named contractor under the $550B US-Japan AI infrastructure framework (up to $332B earmarked for energy)

productsAndServices.name: Data Centers (campus-ecosystem delivery)
productsAndServices.category: Data-center core & shell, power, water and modularization
productsAndServices.description: The dedicated data-center practice sells the ecosystem around the campus: core & shell, power generation and transmission for campuses, water treatment, mission-critical MEP, modularized data centers, and greenfield campus delivery via progressive design-build and early contractor involvement — with >80% of work self-performed (company claim). Client names are not published.
highlights: ENR classifies only ~4% of Kiewit's 2025 revenue as telecom/data-center building work — the AI exposure routes through the 38% power line instead
Modularization and off-site manufacturing emphasized across data-center and power delivery
The differentiation vs interior-heavy DC franchises (DPR, HITT, Turner): Kiewit sells generation, substations, and water — the scopes those GCs subcontract
productsAndServices.positioning: A campus-infrastructure specialist rather than a shell/fit-out GC — complementary to (and occasionally competing with) the building cohort
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Progressive design-build, FEED-to-EPC conversion, early contractor involvement
productsAndServices.roadmap: Scaling with the power book; anonymized project fleet suggests NDA-bound hyperscale work

productsAndServices.name: Transmission, HVDC & Substations
productsAndServices.description: Transmission lines, distribution, substations and switchyards, including the marquee HVDC projects of the era: lead designer/GC on the completed 339-mile, 1,250 MW Champlain Hudson Power Express (Québec to NYC), and a ~$1.7B share (with Quanta) of Invenergy's Grain Belt Express — an 800-mile, 5,000 MW HVDC line billed as the largest transmission project in US history.
highlights: CHPE completed June 2026: ~146 miles of terrestrial route plus the Astoria converter station; 2025 Trenchless Technology Project of the Year
Grain Belt Express Phase 1 construction targeted from 2026 (financing/political status fluid — verify before relying)
Multi-year utility programs, e.g., PacifiCorp distribution: ≥350 miles/year over five years
productsAndServices.positioning: One of the few contractors with completed US HVDC converter-station delivery — the transmission class that moves gigawatts to load centers
productsAndServices.soldThrough: EPC and program contracts with utilities and transmission developers
productsAndServices.roadmap: Data-center-driven transmission demand; Grain Belt execution pending financing clarity

productsAndServices.name: Nuclear (Kiewit Nuclear Solutions)
productsAndServices.description: Kiewit Nuclear Solutions is lead constructor for Oklo's first Aurora powerhouse at Idaho National Laboratory (~75 MWe fast reactor; Sam Altman-backed developer): design, procurement, and construction management focused on non-nuclear scope; ~370 construction jobs; commissioning targeted late 2027-early 2028. Groundbreaking September 2025.
highlights: One of the first US SMR construction seats — the Aurora is among the first advanced reactors to reach construction
No confirmed Kiewit role on TerraPower Natrium, BWXT, or X-energy programs (negative finding — the Oklo seat is the verified relationship)
productsAndServices.positioning: First-mover constructor credential in the reactor class AI hyperscalers are underwriting
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Construction-management and EPC contracts with advanced-reactor developers
productsAndServices.roadmap: Aurora commissioning 2027-28; follow-on Aurora units if the first executes

productsAndServices.name: Heavy Civil, Marine, Water & Industrial (diversified core)
productsAndServices.description: The most diversified book in ENR's top 10: transportation (29% of ENR-counted revenue — bridges, highways, transit, aviation), water/sewer/waste (14%), oil/gas/chemical including LNG delivery, mining, and marine — expanded by the January 2023 acquisition of Weeks Marine (with Healy Tibbitts and McNally), making Kiewit a major US dredging and marine contractor.
highlights: Nine primary markets; in-house design via Kiewit Engineering Group; Mass. Electric Construction for electrical/transit systems
Key Bridge (Baltimore): won the $73M Phase 1 progressive design-build (Aug 2024) but was off-ramped from the ~$1.2B Phase 2 in April 2026 over pricing
Craft pipeline: Kiewit University training center (Omaha, 65,000 sq ft) trains >3,000 learners/year; ~$5B equipment fleet (third-party estimate, low confidence)
productsAndServices.positioning: Cycle ballast at national scale — the diversification that kept Kiewit top-4 while pure-DC builders surged past on the AI wave
productsAndServices.roadmap: Steady-state; growth capital concentrates on power, nuclear, and transmission

recentDevelopments.headline: Champlain Hudson Power Express completed: the 339-mile, 1,250 MW HVDC line from Québec to New York City, with Kiewit as lead designer/GC on ~146 miles of terrestrial route and the Astoria converter station
recentDevelopments.read: A finished US HVDC mega-line is a rare credential — exactly the transmission class that data-center load growth will force more of.

recentDevelopments.headline: Maryland 'off-ramps' Kiewit from the ~$1.2B Francis Scott Key Bridge Phase 2 rebuild after its price proposal 'far exceeded the state's independent cost estimates'; Kiewit completes Phase 1 through end-2026
recentDevelopments.read: A public black eye on the nation's most-watched bridge job — but also a read on pricing discipline: Kiewit held its number in an escalating market ($2B estimate grown to $4.3-5.2B) rather than buy the work.

recentDevelopments.headline: ENR 2026 Top 400: #4 at $15.3B ENR-counted revenue — down from #3 despite growth, passed by STO Building Group's data-center surge; the most diversified mix in the top 10 (38% power, 29% transportation)
recentDevelopments.read: The irony of the AI cycle: Kiewit slipped a rank because the building-side AI plays (STO, DPR, HITT, Mortenson) scaled faster than its power-side exposure — which is larger in dollars but recognized over longer EPC schedules.

strategyRead: 1. (High confidence) We assess Kiewit is the purest power-side play on the AI buildout among top-tier contractors: a stacked ~11 GW gas-EPC book (Homer City 4.5 GW, NRG/GEV ~5.4 GW, Oglethorpe 1.4 GW), completed HVDC delivery (CHPE), the Oklo SMR constructor seat, and a data-center practice that sells campus power/water/shell rather than fit-out. Its 4% ENR telecom mix understates AI exposure that actually routes through the 38% power line.

2. (High confidence) We assess reserved GE Vernova 7HA turbine slots plus TIC's >82 GW gas-delivery track record constitute the scarcest capability set in the AI-power complex: turbine manufacturing capacity, not construction labor, gates gigawatt-class gas through 2030, and Kiewit sits inside the OEM's allocation via the NRG venture. This is a moat rival EPCs cannot quickly replicate.

3. (Moderate confidence) We assess the employee-ownership model (direct stock purchase by selected employees, book-value buy-back on departure — not a conventional ESOP) plus reported ~7.2% net margins reflect a disciplined risk-pricing culture: the Key Bridge off-ramp reads as Kiewit refusing to buy politically visible work below its price, accepting reputational cost to protect the margin engine that funds employee-owner returns. The net-income figure itself is aggregator-sourced and unverified (medium confidence).

4. (Moderate confidence) We assess the fixed-price gas-EPC concentration is the mirror-image risk of the moat: Homer City-class projects at >$10B campus scale against constrained turbine logistics and scarce craft amplify downside on any miss, and an AI-capex pause would strand the growth engine while the diversified book (transportation, water, marine) cushions but does not offset it.

5. (Moderate confidence) We assess Kiewit's opacity is strategic but increasingly costly analytically: no backlog disclosure, no leadership page, dual revenue series (company $18.2B vs ENR $15.3B for 2025 — methodology, not contradiction), and a Wikipedia article flagged for neutrality in January 2026. Counterparties get less visibility into a $18B firm than into public peers a third its size.

6. (Low confidence) We assess the US-Japan framework naming (with Bechtel) could become the largest demand channel of all — up to $332B for energy infrastructure — but no Kiewit projects have been assigned; treat it as optionality, not backlog.

relationships.note: Standing generation venture (with NRG) holding reserved 7HA turbine slots — plus EPC on three GEV-powered gigawatt plants.
relationships.context:
February 2025: NRG, GE Vernova and Kiewit (TIC) formed a generation venture initially targeting ~5.4 GW of combined-cycle plants for data-center demand in ERCOT and PJM, with reserved turbine slots — converting Kiewit's EPC bench into allocated OEM capacity competitors can't match, since turbine slots (not construction labor) gate gigawatt-class gas through 2030.

The delivery record around it: Homer City, PA (EPC for up to 4.5 GW on seven GEV 7HA.02s — the largest US gas plant under construction, powering a >3,200-acre AI campus, first power targeted 2027) and Oglethorpe's 1,425 MW Georgia plant (GEV 7HA.03, COD 2029).

relationships.note: Co-named delivery contractor under the $550B US-Japan AI infrastructure framework.
relationships.context: October 2025: Kiewit and Bechtel were the two US EPC firms named delivery contractors under the $550B US-Japan AI infrastructure framework, with up to $332B earmarked for energy infrastructure. No Kiewit projects have been assigned — the dossier treats it as optionality, not backlog, but the two-firm shortlist itself is the signal.

relationships.note: Building-side AI-cycle peer that scaled faster in the ENR rankings.
relationships.context: Kiewit slipped to #4 in the ENR 2026 Top 400 despite growth because building-side AI plays (STO, DPR, HITT, Mortenson) scaled faster than its power-side exposure — which is larger in dollars but recognized over longer EPC schedules. Different lanes (power EPC vs data-center GC), same AI capex pool.

decisionMakers.name: Rick Lanoha
decisionMakers.title: President & Chief Executive Officer
background: CEO since 2020-01-01 — the sixth CEO in the company's 140+ year history; joined Kiewit part-time in 1986

B.S. construction engineering, University of Nebraska-Omaha; field engineer (Southern California) → District Manager & President of Mass. Electric Construction (Boston, 2003) → Board 2009 → EVP Kiewit Industrial Group → President & COO 2016 → CEO
Founding member of the construction-industry CEO Advisory Council on suicide prevention; visible champion of the 'Under the Hat' craft mental-health program
